correctness.rationale: The proof covers all labelled fixed-weight primitive binary words at every odd half-length m>=3. The repeated-block characterization bounds deleted words by S_m, the Krawtchouk identity establishes a nonzero even-weight gap M_m, and S_m<M_m holds by explicit five-case checks and a valid increasing exponential inequality for m>=13. Complement-pairing forces exactly odd-weight zeros, yielding rank 2^(2m-1) and the complement-invariant image. At odd primes, only two alternating words are excluded; their character sum and selection-count identity prove the full signed spectrum, multiplicities, sharp extrema, and inverse norm. Stirling and an exponentially smaller deletion bound yield the all-odd sharp asymptotic. Two distinct exact-integer checker programs passed: direct 2^(2m)-frequency transforms through m=9 and symbolic prime signed multiplicities through p=13. Finite results are not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: Bounded accessible primary-text and mathematical-record comparisons establish that fixed-density necklace enumeration/indexing, full Hamming-shell Krawtchouk values, and sampling Gram matrices do not directly imply the complete Walsh support of the balanced aperiodic subfamily, or the prime signed-multiplicity and sharp-stability formulas. The central new implication is a strict uniform domination of the whole Fourier perturbation by the nonzero undeleted shell gap. Prior results on unrestricted primitive words cannot be specialized to fixed Hamming weight. Priority risk of unindexed equivalent formulas remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed harmonic-analytic treatment of fixed-density primitive words could contain equivalent multiplier statements.

value.rationale: Fixed-content aperiodic necklaces are a canonical object, and replacing their usual cardinality by the complete Fourier support measures whether the restriction to primitive balanced words creates new information-loss directions. The all-odd theorem settles a natural infinite-family noncancellation question, proves exact recovery on the complement-invariant subspace, and distinguishes rank from exponential ill-conditioning. The prime specialization determines the entire signed spectrum and exact sharp stability, rather than just a finite numerical census.
